dedupe_keys.name: ncfh farm labor data dashboard national center for farmworker health

description: The Farm Labor Data Dashboard is an interactive web tool that brings together nationally available data about farmworkers in the United States from sources such as the Department of Labor and the Department of Agriculture, to show the national landscape of farm labour. It is built by the National Center for Farmworker Health, a private non-profit organisation in Buda, Texas, that has supported farmworker health since 1975. Users can view data at national, state and county level where available and export data. Access is free but by registration: users fill in a form, and NCFH staff review it within two to three days before giving access. Caveats: the page read does not list the exact source tables, years or update schedule, and farmworker counts from national surveys are known to miss seasonal and undocumented workers. For simulation it helps locate farmworker populations, whose housing, language and work patterns make them vulnerable during heat waves, floods and hurricanes, so emergency response and resilience models of agricultural areas can include them. It is related to the North Central Florida farmworker social vulnerability case study record in this catalogue, which maps the same population locally.
